comments.author: @adhisubagio
comments.text:
This documentary provides an in-depth look at Tajikistan, the poorest former Soviet state, highlighting the country's striking contradictions and resilient culture.

Key themes explored include:

Persian Heritage & Beauty Standards: The country maintains deep Persian roots (01:34). Beauty standards are unique, where a natural or painted unibrow is often considered a sign of purity and health (03:40).
Social & Economic Hardships: With many men migrating to Russia for work (09:12), women are the primary backbone of rural communities, managing labor and households (10:50). The country struggles with high poverty, limited electricity in winter (15:54), and expensive marriage customs that have led to practices like bride kidnapping (05:43) and divorce via text message (07:24).
Government Control: The state exerts strict control over daily life, including regulations on religious clothing (banning hijabs), forced beard shaving for men (12:12), and limitations on the number of guests allowed at weddings to prevent financial ruin (14:07).
Infrastructure & Geography: Tajikistan is home to breathtaking, mountainous landscapes and massive engineering projects like the Rogan Dam, which aims to provide energy independence (19:40). It also faces environmental risks, such as the potentially dangerous Usoy Dam (21:13).
Political & Foreign Influence: The country is ruled by a long-standing political family (22:45) and faces significant economic pressure from China, which has become its largest creditor (24:32).
